subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Robot Wiring: Power and Signals
description: A quick, practical guide to Robot Wiring: Power and Signals.

hook.text: Inside a robot arm, bundles of cables carry power, encoder signals, and pneumatic lines through every joint.

buildup.text: Cables must flex millions of times without breaking. Special robot-grade cables use stranded copper and flexible jackets.

discovery.text: Routing cables through the arm interior protects them from snags and damage. External cables catch on everything.

twist.text: Cable failure is one of the top causes of robot downtime. A broken encoder wire stops a million-dollar production line.

climax.text: Newer robots use slip rings and wireless signals to reduce cable fatigue. Fewer wires mean fewer failure points.

punchline.text: The robot's weakest link is often a wire, not a gear.

quiz.question: Why are cables a common cause of robot downtime?
options: They overheat from carrying too much electrical current
They must flex millions of times through joints and eventually break from fatigue
They interfere with the robot's sensors and cause positioning errors
